gaps.id: CITE-1 mechanism: manifest switch plus CITATION.cff subset
gaps.requirement: A 'how to cite' source that stays in each app repository (nothing written twice), is author-controlled, shows a formatted reference rather than a bare DOI, can say 'no publication yet' explicitly, and needs the network only in the snapshot step.
gaps.current: Only the optional `doi` (schema/labconstrictor-app.schema.json:36) rendered as a bare link in the last section. Per app the citation already lives in up to three places (README prose or BibTeX, manifest `doi`, a Zenodo record), and no repo has a CITATION.cff. COMPARISON. (a) manifest `citation` block: least code and the template checker validates it for free, but it retypes what the README, Zenodo and (per the auditor's own step 6) a CITATION.cff already carry, so it would be the fourth copy, and it feeds neither GitHub's 'Cite this repository' nor Zenodo. (c) DOI content negotiation at snapshot time: no retyped data and the registry record is the safest source for papers, but verified problems: cross-host redirects (needs a second HTTP client with an allowlist), per-agency output differences (bioRxiv text without venue, DataCite text with HTML, mangled BibTeX key), registry name parsing that disagrees with the authors' own (Pineda vs Rivera Pineda), no way to say 'no publication' or carry a software archive DOI or version, a DOI minted before the paper is live would presumably 404 and under no-silent-fallbacks unlist the app (not tested), a registry outage must stop the whole fetch (exit 4, like a GitHub outage) which adds a new way for the daily build to fail, and the author cannot correct what is displayed. (b) site reads the app's own CITATION.cff: one standard file per repo that GitHub, Zenodo (subset) and Zotero also read, so the auditor's step 6 and step 2 become the same task; only GitHub is contacted (already the only network host); parsed with load_plain_yaml.
gaps.proposal: RECOMMEND (b), in its smallest form. 1) Manifest, one new optional key, named for merging with the benchmark audit: `citation: cff | none` (enum). `cff` = show the preferred-citation of the repository's root CITATION.cff; `none` = the authors list no publication. No other manifest key is added, so any 'publication', 'references' or 'how_to_cite' key proposed elsewhere should be dropped in favour of this one. `doi` stays valid and keeps its meaning (DOI of the work to cite) but gets `deprecated: true`; `doi` together with `citation` is an error (schema `not: {required: [doi, citation]}` for editors, plus an explicit AppProblem in catalogue because jsonschema's own message for `not` dumps the whole manifest, verified). 2) catalogue.resolve (catalogue.py:91-108) gets one call `read_citation(gh, name, branch, manifest)`: when citation == cff, gh.raw(name, branch, 'CITATION.cff') on the same default branch as the manifest (100 KB cap, GitHub host only), load_plain_yaml (aliases refused), then validate against `$defs/citationFile` placed INSIDE schema/labconstrictor-app.schema.json (no new schema file, so no fourth copy to sync; validator = Draft202012Validator({'$ref': '#/$defs/citationFile', '$defs': schema['$defs']}), tested). 3) Subset (everything else in the file is ignored and never copied, so emails, addresses, contact and references are never stored or shown): top-level cff-version const '1.2.0', title, authors (CFF-required), optional doi (software archive, same DOI pattern as the manifest), and REQUIRED preferred-citation with: type const 'article' (preprints use status), title 1-300 chars, journal 1-100, year integer 1900-2100 (date-published and date-released are NOT read: PyYAML turns them into datetime.date), doi (existing pattern), authors 1-100 of {family-names, given-names, optional name-particle, name-suffix} or {name}, optional volume, issue, start, end, month 1-12, status in {preprint, in-press, advance-online}; title and journal reject { } \ and control characters. A software-only CITATION.cff (no preferred-citation) is rejected with 'use citation: none' until the authors decide how to show software year and version. 4) Snapshot gets app['citation'] = {state: paper|none|doi-only|undeclared, reference: whitelisted dict or null, software_doi: str or null}; bump SNAPSHOT_FORMAT 2 to 3 (config.py:18). 5) Failure behaviour, no new hosts: missing or invalid file, alias, oversize, wrong type -> AppProblem naming CITATION.cff (app left out, named in build/problems.md, shown as a failed check at submission); GitHub outage -> existing FetchError exit 4; the offline build reads only the snapshot. 6) Crossref/DataCite is not in the build. Optional later: a warning-only lint in submit_app.py comparing title and year (never authors) of the CFF against the registry.
repo_and_files: labconstrictor-site: scripts/lcsite/catalogue.py (resolve, new read_citation and whitelist helpers)
gaps.needs_author_decision: Maintainers confirm (b) over (a) and the enum name `citation` (the benchmark audit's fields must not use the same key); whether a software-only CITATION.cff should later be shown.
gaps.rule_conflicts: Vendored schema copies already break 'nothing written twice' by design (streamlit schemas/README.md); this design adds no new file to that list by using $defs. Keeping `doi` vs 'do not accept legacy aliases' (AGENTS.md:60): `doi` is not an alias (own meaning, valid alone, marked deprecated, reported by a warning), and removal date is a maintainers' call. Optional CFF keys must be tested with `in`, never .get(key, default) (AGENTS.md:68). Functions must stay at most 30 lines: split read_citation, whitelist_reference, whitelist_person.

gaps.id: CITE-2 rendering: section, states, version, copy buttons
gaps.requirement: A 'How to cite' section close to 'Using it' with authors, title, venue, year, DOI, Read paper, Copy reference and Copy BibTeX; the app's version visible separately; 'no publication' stated explicitly; escaped; consistent with DESIGN.md.
gaps.current: Cite is a Details row (pages_apps.py:152-153) with no reference, no copy and no version relation; pages for apps without a doi say nothing. lc.js copy handler resets any button label to 'Copy' (lc.js:83-92) and copies only the first <code> of the parent.
gaps.proposal:
New module scripts/lcsite/citation.py (pure functions, under 300 lines): reference_text(ref) in one house style, APA-like (prototype output matches Crossref APA for authors, year and title for NucleiSky, CellTracksColab, VLab4Mic; initials from given-names, 'Family, I., ..., & Family, I. (2026). Title. Journal, volume(issue), start. https://doi.org/DOI'); bibtex(ref) (@article, key = slugify(first family)+year+first title word, escape & % $ # _ because braces and backslashes are refused by the schema); section(app) and block(ref, heading, id) returning escaped HTML (every value through text.esc). PLACEMENT in page_app: p.add(citation.section(app)) right after using_section and before downloads_table; h2 id='cite' 'How to cite'; delete the Cite row from details_list. STATES (explicit, never silent): paper (citation: cff): lead 'If you use {name} in your research, the authors ask you to cite this article:' ('this preprint:' when status is preprint; the wording attributes the request to the authors); reference in

; two ghost small buttons 'Copy reference' and 'Copy BibTeX' (data-copy); action link lc-go 'Read the paper' or 'Read the preprint' to https://doi.org/{quoted doi} (a link navigates, buttons only copy: DESIGN.md:38); BibTeX shown in

BibTeX. none (citation: none): 'The authors list no publication for {name} yet. If you use it, name the app and its version and link its repository' with the GitHub pill; no copy button. doi-only (legacy doi, no citation): 'The authors give this DOI: doi:... ' with an action link 'Open doi:...' plus a build WARNING 'add CITATION.cff and citation: cff'. undeclared (neither): 'The authors have not said how to cite this app.' plus a build WARNING (this is the 'Not stated' pattern already used for License). VERSION, always separate and never taken from the CFF: a line 'Version {release tag}, released {date}. Cite the version you ran; all versions are on the GitHub releases page.' built from release['tag'] and published_at (omitted for apps with no release); if the CFF has a top-level doi, add 'Software archive: doi:...' (neutral label, the site cannot know whether it is a concept or version DOI). lc.js: restore each button's own label after 'Copied' and let a button name its source with data-copy-from= (about 4 lines); lc.css: .lc-ref as normal-font prose, BibTeX monospace and wrapping; DESIGN.md: add a 'Citation block' pattern in the same pull request (DESIGN.md:4 says no pattern, add it first); check_site.author_strings: scan app['citation'] as well as app['manifest'] so unescaped citation text fails the build. Optional S follow-up: schema.org `citation` in jsonld(app).
gaps.needs_author_decision: Wording of the lead sentences and of the 'no publication' sentence; house reference style (APA-like proposed) versus the journals' own.
gaps.rule_conflicts: DESIGN.md: a page has at most one filled button (none used), a card has no button (not a card), outside links open in a new tab (automatic via page.py). Escape app-written text, never render it as HTML or Markdown (AGENTS.md:71): the CFF `message` and `abstract` are therefore never shown. pages_apps.py is 208 lines, the new code lives in citation.py to stay under 300.

gaps.id: CITE-3 LabConstrictor itself: block, footer, duplicate DOI

gaps.current: The preprint is shown nowhere on the site. The footer links the Zenodo version DOI 10.5281/zenodo.20758747, which is version 0.0.2 of concept 10.5281/zenodo.19074199 (template_version is 0.1.15, no GitHub releases or tags), and the same DOI is also in the unused data/site.yaml:15.
gaps.proposal: Source: inline in data/site.yaml (hand-written site data), NOT a root CITATION.cff in the template, because the template is copied into every app (AGENTS.md:28) and the initialiser only rewrites README.md, so every new app would inherit a CITATION.cff presenting the LabConstrictor preprint as the app's citation; the ecosystem card for the template is already inline for the same reason. Shape: `citation: {paper: <same fields as a CFF preferred-citation, validated by the same $defs/reference>, software_doi: <DOI>}` replacing the dead links.citation_doi. Facts verified for the paper entry: title 'Packaging Jupyter notebooks as installable desktop apps using LabConstrictor', status preprint, journal arXiv, year 2026, doi 10.48550/arXiv.2603.10704, author order Hidalgo-Cenalmor, Rivera Pineda, Saraiva, Henriques, Jacquemet (name spellings: see CITE-6). Render with the same citation.block(): a band with id='cite' and h2 'Cite LabConstrictor' on the home page (pages_site.page_home), lead taken from the template README ('If you use LabConstrictor in your research, please cite the project'), reference, Copy reference, Copy BibTeX, 'Read the preprint'; below it a lc-small line 'Software archive: doi:...' (separate from the paper) and a text link 'Using an app for your results? Each app page has a How to cite section' to apps/. Footer: replace the hard-coded DOI link in overrides/main.html:100 by an internal link to the home #cite (label 'Cite LabConstrictor' unchanged; an in-site link opens in the same tab and check_site validates the anchor); delete links.citation_doi. No new page, so the 3-click reachability rule is unaffected. Add a unit test that data/site.yaml's paper entry passes the reference schema.
gaps.needs_author_decision: Which DOI is the 'software archive': concept 10.5281/zenodo.19074199 (all versions) or the 0.0.2 version DOI now in the footer; whether the home block should say apps built with LabConstrictor also cite the preprint (the README says 'if you use LabConstrictor in your research, please cite the project'; the auditor's rule 'app results -> cite the app, discussing LabConstrictor -> cite the preprint' is the auditor's, not the authors' stated policy).
gaps.rule_conflicts: The template's README holds the same citation as prose, so this one item is written twice (README and data/site.yaml); accepted by the existing precedent of the inline template card (AGENTS.md:28) and to be listed in AGENTS.md 'Sources of truth'. A hand-written site.yaml entry is allowed (AGENTS.md:32).

gaps.requirement: The new manifest key and CITATION.cff are checked where authors work, and every listed app declares its citation, without breaking apps that exist today.
gaps.current: Template origin/main has a vendored schema copy, check_app_manifest.py (existence check only for icon and screenshots), docs/app_manifest.md and migration resources up to v0_1_14_to_v0_1_15; LabConstrictor_streamlit has another schema copy and a form that writes labconstrictor-app.yaml; none of the six apps has a citation declaration or a CITATION.cff.
gaps.proposal: TEMPLATE (CellMigrationLab/LabConstrictor, PR from a fresh branch off origin/main): copy the new schema into .tools/schema/ via a new migration v0_1_15_to_v0_1_16 (same MANAGED_FILES pattern as v0_1_14_to_v0_1_15, resources folder, manifest.yaml entry, version bump); extend .tools/python/check_app_manifest.py by about 15 lines: when manifest citation == 'cff', add 'CITATION.cff' to the files-exist check and validate it against $defs/citationFile (annotation file=CITATION.cff) so a typo is caught in the app's own pull request instead of unlisting the app at the next daily site build; .tools/docs/app_manifest.md gets a 'How to cite' section with the `citation` key and a CITATION.cff example (it is a site guide and migration-tied: wording must pass check_design generic-link rules, see KNOWN_EXCEPTIONS). Do not add a root CITATION.cff to the template (inherited by every app, see CITE-3). gaps.requirement: Missing or malformed citation information is reported, never silent; new submissions must declare; existing listed apps are not unlisted by the rollout.
gaps.current: submit_app.check (submit_app.py:47-59) reuses catalogue.resolve and prints warnings; the daily build lists per-app warnings in build/problems.md (the icon case). Nothing today distinguishes 'no publication' from 'forgot'.
gaps.proposal: Phase 1 (site ships first): `citation` optional; apps with neither `citation` nor `doi` get state undeclared plus a catalogue warning ('declare citation: cff or citation: none'); apps with only `doi` get state doi-only plus a warning ('add CITATION.cff'); both are reported in build/problems.md and the daily issue (AGENTS.md:62 allows reported warnings for optional fields). submit_app.check adds two hard failures for NEW submissions only: no `citation` -> 'declare citation: cff or citation: none'; `doi` alone -> 'doi is deprecated: use citation: cff'. Phase 2 (maintainers pick the date once the six apps are migrated): add 'citation' to the schema `required` list in the three schema copies and delete the doi-only and undeclared states. Tests (tests/test_citation.py, each with a failure case, annotations and docstrings per AGENTS.md:66): the three verified drafts parse and render; citation: cff with no file -> AppProblem naming CITATION.cff; alias in the file -> AppProblem; type: book, braces in title, missing doi, year as string -> AppProblem; doi plus citation -> AppProblem; <script> and quotes in title/author/journal come out escaped in HTML and in the copy text; unknown CFF keys (email, contact) never reach the snapshot; version line uses the release tag and ignores CFF version; no-release app omits it; none, doi-only and undeclared states each render their sentence and (for the last two) a warning; SNAPSHOT_FORMAT mismatch stops the build; build_site never opens a socket (existing offline rule).
